# VVT and cam solenoid issues

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Check that the accelerator pedal is fully released, then cycle the ignition switch on for two to ten-second intervals. [t22]

[Partial] Ensure voltage, temperature, and pedal position are correct then perform accelerator learning steps. [t22]

[Partial] VITs are the Variable Intake Air Solenoids. [t30]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Ensure battery voltage is more than 12.9V at idle.
2. Confirm engine coolant temperature is between 70°C and 100°C (158°F - 212°F).
3. Set the PNP switch to ON position.
4. [Partial] Turn off any electric loads like air conditioner, headlamps, or rear window defogger.
5. Ensure steering wheel is in a neutral straight-ahead position.
6. Verify vehicle speed is stopped and transmission is warmed up (or drive for 10 minutes if no CONSULT-II).
7. [Partial] Perform Accelerator Pedal Released Position Learning first.
8. [Partial] Perform Throttle Valve Closed Position Learning next.
9. Start the engine and warm it to normal operating temperature.
10. Turn ignition switch OFF and wait at least 10 seconds.
11. Confirm accelerator pedal is fully released, then turn ignition ON and wait 3 seconds.
12. Repeat quickly five times within a 5-second window: fully depress accelerator, then fully release it.
13. Wait 7 seconds, then fully depress the accelerator pedal and hold for approximately 20 seconds until MIL blinks solid.
14. Fully release the accelerator pedal within 3 seconds after the MIL turns ON.

_Procedure reported by [t22]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t22] [Partial]</summary>

1. Check that the accelerator pedal is fully released.
2. Turn the ignition switch ON and wait at least 2 seconds.
3. Turn the ignition switch OFF and wait at least 10 seconds.
4. [Partial] Turn the ignition switch ON again and wait at least 2 seconds.

</details>

## Tools

- [Partial] Clock or stopwatch [t22]

## Parts

- VIAS, Variable Intake Air Solenoid [t30]

## Tips & gotchas

- Count time accurately with a clock if not using CONSULT-II. [t22]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Failing to wait long enough between ignition cycles. [t22]
- [Partial] Not fully releasing the accelerator pedal before starting. [t22]
- Missing any preparation condition for even a moment, which cancels learning. [t22]
- [Partial] Not disconnecting the battery when cleaning a nasty throttle body unit that had compensated previously. [t22]
